description: TEST SET. The 30 synthetic user utterances from the thesis dataset (chatbot_data_preparation_en), five per intent, with their original labels in "intent". They are used only to measure intent recognition (kb/evaluate-chat.mjs). They are never loaded into the database and never vote, so the chatbot is always tested on questions it has not seen. "secondary" marks a question that the dataset author judges to belong to two intents. It was added on 2026-10-12, after the first evaluation runs, so the evaluation always reports the strict figure ("intent" only) next to the relaxed one ("intent" or "secondary").

examples.text: What is academic burnout and its symptoms?
Is burnout the same as normal stress?
Why are IT students prone to burnout?
Does burnout affect my GPA?
What is the difference between physical fatigue and burnout?
My PBL projects are piling up, what should I do?
examples.secondaryReason: Describes a heavy load and asks what to do about it; managing time is part of the answer.

examples.text: What does Temporal Demand mean in the questionnaire?
I am frustrated, my coding always has errors.
examples.secondaryReason: The thesis dataset files it under workload ("a high cognitive load"), and frustration is one of the six NASA-TLX dimensions. The dataset author also reads it as the student voicing a strained state rather than describing a load, and the knowledge base (WL-04, Gumasing et al., 2022) reports that students with more frustration also report more exhaustion.

examples.text: Why is my Physical Demand score high even though I just sit?

examples.secondaryReason: Clashing assignments raise the workload and are also a scheduling problem.
